description.narrative: AfricaMuseum Cooperation programme is dedicated to safeguarding and celebrating Africa’s rich cultural and natural heritage in alignment with SDG 11.4, aiming to protect and transmit this legacy while empowering African communities through access to their heritage. The AfricaMuseum serves as a hub for cultural preservation and dialogue to ensure that Africa’s rich heritage is valued and passed on for the present and future generations. Focusing on natural hazards and related risks, the AfricaMusuem´s cooperation programme supports SDG 11.5’s aim to substantially reduce the impact of disasters on human lives, especially among vulnerable populations, and decrease economic losses caused by disasters and natural hazards (Land slides, flooding, volcanic eruptions etc.). Furthermore, it contributes to SDG 13.1 by promoting efforts to enhance resilience and adaptive capacity to climate-related hazards and natural disasters globally In the pursuit of a fair, inclusive, sustainable, and equal world, AfricaMuseum strives to bring about transformative societal shifts through culture and to create a global community that is well-informed, engaged, and committed to the shared vision of a sustainable future. Stereotypes and knowledge gaps are challenged while empowering individuals to embrace diversity, support inclusivity, and actively contribute to sustainable societies Natural resources have an improved contribution to sustainable development The AfricaMuseum´s cooperation programme contributes to the integration of research-driven strategies into policies and daily practices at local, national and global levels, resulting in effective and sustainable management of natural resources including geo-resources, forest and freshwater systems Embracing the One Health Approach, the AfricaMuseum cooperation programme focusses on the mapping and monitoring of pests, parasites and vectors and the health of the ecosystem to better understand related risks. This knowledge is used to develop targeted strategies that directly address risks at the intersection of humans, animals and their various environment and aligns with the aim to improve health and promote sustainable food production
